## 8e8d21720efb

**Finding: global color frequency is a strong canonical shortcut for the intended local-connectivity rule.** The rival “keep every nonzero cell whose color appears at least twice anywhere in the grid” fits all **5/5 canonical pairs**. It also matches the intended transform on **274/300 sampled ordinary inputs**. In explicit three-demonstration probes (same seed, three consecutive generated samples), it survives all demonstrations in **79/100 easy**, **91/100 medium**, and **97/100 hard** lessons. The exact sampling policy and examples are retained in `checks/audit/8e8d21720efb/fit_probe.json` and `checks/audit/8e8d21720efb/lesson_probe.json`.

A validator-lawful counterexample is an `8×9` grid with two distant color-4 singleton cells at `(1,1)` and `(6,7)`. `self_check` returns no errors. The canonical Racket rule erases both because neither has a same-color cardinal neighbor; the frequency rival keeps both. Exact input, rival output, and source-bound Racket output are in `checks/audit/8e8d21720efb/` (`input.json`, `rival_output.json`, `racket.json`, `probe.json`).

Ordinary generation assigns distinct colors to nominal components. Accidental shape overwrites sometimes fragment a repeated-color blob and refute the shortcut, which explains the 26/300 single-input disagreements, but this is sparse and not expressed as a semantic contract. A deliberate same-color disconnected-component axis or witness would teach the locality requirement much more reliably. The current `self_check` is also too weak to enforce the documented blob/singleton mix.
